# Tâche : MM-03.3 — jalon 1, passe 6 (arènes par détenteur, store, transfert, progrès, protection des paramètres)

## Git
Même branche `formal/access_model_0.1`, à la suite. Pas de merge, pas de PR. Tout sous `formal/`. `Ern/MM02.lean` inchangé. Spec jointe : MM-03.3 v0.2, non copiée ; arbitrages A1–A11, B1–B10, C1–C9, D1–D4 en vigueur, sauf ce que les arbitrages ci-dessous remplacent ; ceux-ci font foi.

## Langue
Code, docstrings, commentaires, messages de commit en anglais. Rapport en français.

## Arbitrages (font foi)
F1. Arènes par détenteur (remplace la phrase de D3 sur le détenteur de `internal`).
  - `newArena storage internal` : `internal` est nommée par l'appelant.
  - Préconditions : `internal` active, `Modify`, `ExercisableAt … .modify` ; détenue par un emplacement (la valeur arène) ; empreinte de `internal` = empreinte de `storage` ; aucune arène vivante n'a déjà `internal` pour `internal`.
  - La valeur arène est le détenteur de `internal`, partout où le module lit aujourd'hui le propriétaire du stockage (`MetaRight`, `arenaValue`).
  - Retirer `arenaInternal`, `IsInternalFor` et sa règle de sorte d'autorité, ainsi que la garde par indice d'emplacement.
  - `issue` ne change aucun propriétaire (inchangé).
F2. `OwnedStorage` retiré de `newArena` : le stockage peut être un local, un statique, une racine allouée ou un bloc. Théorème `live_arena_storage_usable` : sur un état atteint, le stockage d'une arène vivante est utilisable (corollaire attendu de `NoDangling`).
F3. Statiques : l'élément propriétaire reste permis. `StaticPinnedBottom` porte sur les feuilles d'emplacements possédés directement par le cadre 0. `static_not_owned_by_frame0` reste comme témoin de comportement légal.
F4. `store a p : ok | reject` — écriture d'une référence dans une valeur.
  - Préconditions : `a` active, **dérivée** (`a.origin ≠ none`), détenue par le cadre courant ; `p` utilisable ; `Modify` exerçable sur `p` ; `a` ne couvre aucune feuille de `p` ni de son stockage possédé ; `AnchorOrder` vérifié pour l'ancre ajoutée (cadre de l'ancre effective de `a` = cadre de `p` ou un de ses ancêtres).
  - Effet : détenteur de `a` := `p` ; `a` ajoutée aux ancres de `p` ; feuilles de `p` := `Init`.
  - `release` d'une autorité détenue par un emplacement `q` la retire des ancres de `q` dans la même transition. `endUse` inchangé (il supprime déjà les dépendances).
  - Pas d'opération inverse. `store` est un pas de `Reachable`. `RootHeld` n'est pas affaibli.
F5. `TransferPre` exige des empreintes de source et de destination disjointes. Si une clause existante l'implique déjà, ajouter la clause explicite et prouver la redondance ; ne rien retirer.
F6. `call_protects_params_safe`.
  - Enregistrement fantôme `callParams : Frame → List AuthorityId`, fixé par `enterFrame`, jamais modifié, lu par aucune opération.
  - Énoncé : pour un état atteint de pile `f :: F₀`, toute autorité exerçable par le cadre courant, ou par un cadre appelé par `f` transitivement, qui couvre une feuille de l'empreinte d'une autorité `Modify` de `callParams f` est cette autorité ou un de ses descendants, que le paramètre soit actif ou non. La preuve découle des règles existantes (A2, O3.2) ; `callParams` ne sert qu'à l'énoncé.
  - Docstring : accès sûrs seulement ; ni pointeurs bruts, ni suspension.
F7. Progrès, en deux variantes, chacune construite depuis `S3.init` par des pas de `Reachable`.
  - (a) Cycle sur nœuds entiers : deux nœuds dans deux blocs d'une même arène ; `store` dans A d'une autorité `Modify` dérivée sur le bloc de B, puis `store` dans B d'une autorité `Modify` dérivée sur le bloc de A. Attendu : le second `store` est rejeté. Rapporter la clause en cause.
  - (b) Cycle sur champs disjoints : chaque nœud a deux champs, `data` et `link` ; `store` dans `A.link` d'une vue `Modify` sur `B.data`, puis dans `B.link` d'une vue `Modify` sur `A.data`. Attendu : construction acceptée ; démontage par `release` des deux autorités stockées, `endUse` des nœuds, puis `reset` de l'arène accepté.
  - Un verdict obtenu différent est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause. Aucune conclusion d'impossibilité sans preuve : une séquence non trouvée est un résultat ouvert, pas une interdiction.

## Étapes (un commit par étape)
1. F1, F2 : `newArena` réécrit, `MetaRight` et `arenaValue` par détenteur, garde par `internal`, `live_arena_storage_usable`. Préservation et invariant des états atteints réénoncés ; `nested_same_value` retiré ou réénoncé.
2. F3 : `StaticPinnedBottom` sur la possession directe ; `staticPinned_reached` et `static_pinned_never_exits` réénoncés.
3. F4 : `store`, `release` modifié, préservation de `WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ ArenaInv` ; `store_root_rejected` ; `store_escape_rejected_at_transfer` (une valeur tenant une autorité dérivée d'un local du cadre courant ne peut être transférée vers un cadre plus ancien).
4. F5, F6 : clause de `transfer` ; `callParams`, `call_protects_params_safe`, forme transitive.
5. F7 et cas, avec un jumeau positif pour chaque rejet :
   - arène imbriquée : `reset` du parent `reject` tant que l'enfant vit ; `endUse` de la valeur enfant, puis `reset` du parent → `ok` ;
   - arène sur un tampon local : `derive Modify` sur le tampon, `store` dans la valeur arène, `newArena`, deux `issue` → `ok` ; `transfer` de la valeur arène vers l'appelant → `reject` au `transfer` ;
   - arène sur une allocation possédée par sa valeur, rendue à l'appelant → `ok` ;
   - `x2` : `newArena` sur la partie unique d'une racine avec cette racine pour `internal` → `ok` ; seconde arène sur la même racine → `reject` ;
   - vue sur un tableau local stockée dans une structure, puis `transfer` de la structure vers l'appelant → `reject` au `transfer` ; vers un autre local du même cadre → `ok` ;
   - `store` d'une racine → `reject` ;
   - `store`, puis `endUse` de la valeur qui détient l'origine → `reject` ; `release` de l'autorité stockée, puis ce même `endUse` → `ok` ;
   - `transfer(x, x.f)` → `reject` ; jumeau : `transfer(x.f, tmp)` puis `transfer(tmp, x)` → `ok` ;
   - non-vacuité de F6 : la racine de l'appelant couvre l'empreinte du paramètre et n'est pas exerçable par l'appelé ; paramètre libéré puis accès tenté → `reject` ; deux appels imbriqués ;
   - F7 (a) et (b).

## Hors périmètre
Pool de handles, jalon 2, concurrence, flot de contrôle, suspension, `defer`, obligation de libération, syntaxe, corpus MM3-H complet (jalon 3).

## Règles
Zéro `sorry` ; `#print axioms` au plus {propext, Quot.sound} ; aucun `noncomputable` ; `lake build` sans avertissement ; docstrings citant la clause ou l'arbitrage ; rien d'inventé ; aucun énoncé affaibli, tout changement justifié ; revue adverse, avec une lecture dédiée à F1, F4 et F7 ; contre-exemples conservés.

## Livrable
Module commité ; `formal/reports/MM03_v0.1_p6.md` : sections (a)–(o) comme en passe 5, plus (p) résultats de F7 (a) et (b) : verdicts, séquence de démontage, ou pas rejeté et clause en cause.

===== F1 V0 confirmed minor
TITLE Case-16 docstring is now false: since F4, a value can hold a derived access that is not an issued block
REASONING The docstring at formal/Ern/MM03.lean:8673-8677 ends with a general claim: "In the model, a value holds a derived access only as a block issued to it: `derive` and `split` give the current frame as holder." It was written in 24f23b8 (pass 5, step 5), and pass 6 did not change it. F4 adds `store`, a `Reachable` step (`| store` at line 7297), and `storeEff` (line 1221) sets `holder := .place p` on an authority that `StorePre` requires to be derived (`a.origin ≠ none`). I reran the reviewer's c3.lean and it compiles. I also showed that the module's own lb2 is a reached state: j2.lean proves `Reachable K0 [] lb2` (enter1, derive, enter, derive 3 2, store 7 1), and in lb2, `(lb2.A[7]?).map (origin, holder, mode, active) = some (some 3, .place 1, .modify, true) ∧ lb2.arenas = []` holds by `decide`. So on a reached state, place 1 holds an active, derived `Modify` access while no arena exists, and that access cannot be an issued block. The sentence is false under F4.
FIX In formal/Ern/MM03.lean, in the case-16 docstring (lines 8676-8677), replace the last sentence with: "In the model, a value holds a derived access either as a block issued to it or, since F4, as an authority stored into it by `store`; `derive` and `split` give the current frame as holder. Case 16 is modelled here by an issued block." Alternatively, delete the sentence.

===== F1 V1 refuted minor
TITLE x2 case 'second arena on the same root -> reject' is tested only when the same internal is named; a second arena on the same root storage with another internal is reachable and accepted
REASONING The finding says the `reject` verdict holds under only one reading of the brief ("seconde arène sur la même racine → reject"). I checked the state of the case itself: `newArenaEff x2 4 3`, the state right after the first arena. There, every second `newArena` whose storage is the root 3 or its single part 4 is rejected, whatever the internal. `decide` proves this for every index below `A.length`, and an index past `A.length` fails the `OptP … False` clause. The reason is that root 3 is the only active `Modify` authority held by a place that covers [4], and the existing arena already uses it as `internal`. So in the case as briefed, the verdict is `reject` under both readings, and no verdict depends on a reading chosen by the implementer. The reviewer's t3 is a different scenario. It adds a `derive` and a `store` that the brief's case does not contain, and accepting it follows directly from F1's text, not from an interpretation: "aucune arène vivante n'a déjà `internal` pour `internal`" and "Retirer … la garde par indice d'emplacement". The module already has two live arenas over the same leaf [4] (x5: (3,3) and (4,4)). Also, the reading is not silent: the module's x2 docstring states it, "A second arena with the same root as `internal`, here on the root place 3, is rejected". No real defect remains.
FIX None required. If desired, the report may note that in the x2 case state every second arena on storage 3 or 4 is rejected for every internal.

===== F4 V0 confirmed major
TITLE store_escape_rejected_at_transfer only covers an authority anchored on src itself, not one stored in a field of src
REASONING I reproduced this finding. The theorem's hypothesis `ha : a ∈ s.D src` (formal/Ern/MM03.lean:5898) covers only anchors of src itself. `transfer` moves `depsOf s src`, the anchors of src and of all its parts (transferEff, MM03.lean:1008-1016; depsOf, MM03.lean:709, MM-03.3.6). The proof already goes through `depsOf`: `hin` builds `a ∈ depsOf s src` from `.inl rfl`. So the narrower domain is not needed to get a proof. The brief's step 3 says « une valeur tenant une autorité dérivée d'un local du cadre courant ne peut être transférée vers un cadre plus ancien », and storing into a field is the normal way a structure holds a view (step-5 case « vue ... stockée dans une structure »; F7 (b) `A.link`). The only instance in the module, vw3, stores into the structure place 2 itself, so the field case has no theorem. AGENTS.md asks a statement to be neither stronger nor weaker than its source, and this one is weaker for no reason.
FIX Module, MM03.lean:5897-5911: replace `(ha : a ∈ s.D src)` with `(ha : a ∈ depsOf s src)`. Delete `have hsrc := hpre.1` and make the `hin` proof `simp only [transferEff, ↓reduceIte]; exact List.mem_append_right _ ha`. Update the docstring: "a value `src`, one of whose parts (`src` included) is anchored on `a` (`depsOf`, MM-03.3.6)". `vw3_escape_rejected` needs no change: its `(by decide)` proves the new hypothesis, as checked in judge.lean. Optionally add the field case fw0..fw3 from esc.lean as a case with a positive twin. In the report's statement-change table, record that the statement is stronger.

===== F4 V1 confirmed major
TITLE The brief's "value holding" statement is false on a reached state (issued block); the anchor-only form hides this without reporting it
REASONING I reproduced this finding. Read with « tenant » = holder, the brief's step-3 statement is false on a reached state. In lb5, local 5 of the current frame 2 holds the Modify block 8. Block 8 comes from `internal` 7, which comes from root 3 of the local buffer 2, and root 3 is held by frame 2. `issueEff` (MM03.lean:6036) sets `holder := .place dst` but never adds the block to `D dst`, so `lb5.D 5 = []`. `transfer 5 0` to the caller's result (frame 1) is accepted, and block 8 ends up held by `.place 0`. Only the following `exitFrame` rejects. The module itself reads « holding » as holder: MM03.lean:8673-8677 says « Return of a value holding a derived `Modify` access ... In the model, a value holds a derived access only as a block issued to it ». The theorem quantifies over anchors (`a ∈ s.D src`), which matches holding only for authorities placed by `store`. Narrowing the domain this way is exactly what AGENTS.md asks to be reported with a concrete example (« stop and report the exact passage with a concrete example »; « Never ... narrow a theorem's domain to obtain a proof »). Decision (9) states the anchor form but not that the holder form is false. The module docstring (MM03.lean:5891-5896) does not mention it either. The pass-6 report is not written yet, so the gap is in decision (9) as stated.
FIX Report item, pass-6 report, open questions (e) and decision (9). Give the holder reading's counterexample: lb5, step `transfer 5 0` accepted (`TransferStep K0 5 0 lb5 (.ok …)`), block 8 then held by place 0 of frame 1, rejection only at `exitFrame` (ExitPre clause 3). Ask for an arbitration on MM-03.3.1 « Un accès temporaire ne peut être prolongé simplement en le stockant dans un cadre plus ancien » and the step-3 statement. The question: does « tenant » mean only authorities placed and anchored by `store`, or should `issue` anchor the block on its destination, or should `transfer` check the derived authorities it moves to another holder (O4)? Optionally keep lb5 / `transfer 5 0` in the module as a recorded counterexample, as the brief's rule « contre-exemples conservés » asks. The docstring at MM03.lean:8676 (« a value holds a derived access only as a block issued to it ») predates F4 and should mention `store` there.

===== F7 V0 partly minor
TITLE F7 (a): the arbitrated rules accept the second store, which the brief expected to be rejected; the only clause that could reject it is HasRight, and it holds through the first stored authority
REASONING I reran /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/rev12/f7/f7a.lean and f7c.lean and both compile clean. Every StorePre clause holds for `store 8 6` in fa7. 7 is the only witness of HasRight fa7 .modify 6, and it is exercisable only through 8. In fa8, 7 and 8 are not exercisable, and ¬HasRight holds at both modes on 5 and on 6. Under the alternative reading (ga6/ga7), the second store is accepted too. S3.ExercisableAt.held (MM03.lean:765-771) matches B2 word for word, including the place-held case. B2: "ou détenue par un emplacement p tel qu'une autorité exerçable au mode m ait un mode effectif ≥ m sur toute l'empreinte de p". No reading of F4's other clauses rejects the step. B (place 6) holds nothing in fa7, so the coverage clause cannot catch the cycle, and every frame involved is frame 1. The cause is therefore right: a spec defect, since F7 (a)'s expectation contradicts F4 + B2.

It is not a defect of the module, and it is not new. The brief asks for exactly this outcome to be reported: "Un verdict obtenu différent est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause". The docstring of progress_cycle_whole_nodes (MM03.lean:9198-9201) already says "Expected: the second store rejected. Obtained: accepted." It also names the state fa7 and explains the mechanism ("7, held by A, is exercisable through 8 ... `HasRight` on B holds"). Decision (8) declares it as well. "The clause the arbiter most likely expected to fail" is a conjecture, not evidence. Only a report item remains, so the severity drops from major to minor.
FIX No module change. Report item for section (p) of MM03_v0.1_p6.md:
- F7 (a) verdict: accepted at fa7 -> fa8 (`StoreStep 8 6 fa7 (.ok fa8)`).
- No StorePre clause fails. The clause that admits the cycle is F4's "Modify exerçable sur p" (HasRight). Under B2's place-held rule it is witnessed only by 7, which is exercisable through 8, the authority being stored.
- Rejecting the step needs a new arbitrage: either exclude rights that are justified through `a` itself, or add a cycle check to store. This is a semantic change, not a modeling choice.

===== F7 V1 partly minor
TITLE progress_cycle_whole_nodes docstring presents rejections as effects of the cycle, but two of them already occur before it; its permanence is unproven
REASONING Reproduced. The statement (MM03.lean:9216-9222) proves only one-step rejections in fa8, plus the exit facts. The rejections the docstring lists after the colon do not depend on the cycle. f7a.lean (compiles) gives `ResetAtStep K0 0 0 fa4 .reject` and `EndUseStep K0 2 fa7 .reject`, while `ReleaseStep 8 fa7` is ok. My own check, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/rev12/f7judge/j1.lean, finds endUse 3 rejected even in fa5, before any store (`decide (EndUsePre K0 fa5 3) = false`). As a one-step fact, the rejection of endUse/reset in fa8 is no different from the one in fa7. Its only added content would be that it is permanent, and nothing proves that. My one-step probe in j1.lean finds no release accepted in fa8 and endUse accepted only for 1. That still leaves the other operations and longer sequences, so the question stays open. The finding overstates in one place: the docstring is not literally false. Read as statements about fa8, each listed rejection is proven, and "The exit of frame 1 releases both" does not say "only". What reproduces is the misleading causal colon and the unproven deadlock reading, which the brief's rule covers: "une séquence non trouvée est un résultat ouvert".
FIX Reword the docstring at MM03.lean:9200-9202: "In `fa8`, neither 7 nor 8 is exercisable, and `release` of 7 or 8, `endUse` of 2 or 3 and `reset` are rejected. The `endUse` and `reset` rejections already hold before the second store (reset from `fa4`), where 8 could still be released first. Whether frame 1 can free 7 or 8 before its exit is open. The exit releases both." Repeat the open question in report section (p).

===== F7 V2 confirmed minor
TITLE progress_cycle_whole_nodes docstring: 'each state ... with a non-empty list of arenas' is false for fa0 and fa1
REASONING Reproduced. f7c.lean compiles and proves `fa0.arenas = [] ∧ fa1.arenas = []` by decide. f7a.lean's #eval gives (0, 0, 1) for fa0, fa1 and fa2. fa0 and fa1 are states of the run (r0, r1 in the proof), so "Each state is reached from `S3.init []`, with a non-empty list of arenas" is false for them. The theorem states non-emptiness only for fa8. The wording comes from the pass-5 brief (task_mm03_p5.md:30, "avec une liste d'arènes non vide à chaque état vérifié"), which applied to cases 16 and n4, not to F7. The docstring therefore claims more than the facts.
FIX Replace the sentence with: "Each state is reached from `S3.init []`; the list of arenas is non-empty from `fa2` (after `newArena`) on." Alternatively, keep only the stated fact: "`fa8` has a non-empty list of arenas."

===== F7 V3 partly minor
TITLE F7 (b) teardown verdict depends on decision (8), where 'node' means the region place for the stores and the block-holding local for endUse
REASONING The cited facts reproduce: f7b.lean compiles with `EndUseStep K0 5 fb9 .reject`, `EndUseStep K0 8 fb9 .reject`, `¬ EndUseAccessOK fb9 5 5`, `HasRight fb9 .modify 5` and `ResetAtStep K0 0 0 fb9 .reject`. The brief's literal sequence (release the two stored authorities, endUse of the nodes, reset) therefore passes only when 'nodes' at endUse means the values 2 and 3. That depends on decision (8). The finding itself says the decision is declared, so it is not silent.

One claim is refuted: "The implementer's reading is the only one under which the expected 'reset accepted' can be reached." Under the alternative reading, the blocks 5 and 6 can be released in fb9. After that, endUse of the node places 5 and 8 is accepted and the reset is accepted, and the reset is accepted even straight after the two block releases (j1.lean). Reset is reachable under both readings. What differs is whether the brief's exact sequence passes. This is a report item, not a module defect.
FIX No module change. Add to report section (p), next to decision (8), a request for the arbiter to confirm that 'endUse des nœuds' means the values holding the blocks (2 and 3). Also report the alternative reading, where nodes are the places 5 and 8:
- The literal sequence is rejected at `endUse 5` in fb9. Clause: EndUseAccessOK (A2/O3.2), because block 5, held by the live place 2, covers the ending leaves 6 and 7.
- The longer sequence `release 5`, `release 6`, `endUse 5`, `endUse 8`, `reset` is accepted.

===== F356 V0 confirmed minor
TITLE F5: redundancy of the disjointness clause with the init clauses is neither proven nor reported
REASONING F5 (task_mm03_p6.md:23) says: "Si une clause existante l'implique déjà, ajouter la clause explicite et prouver la redondance ; ne rien retirer." TransferPre (MM03.lean:1164-1166) already has two clauses that imply `¬ overlap s.P src dst`: `∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, s.I l = .init` and `∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init`. A leaf in both footprints would have to be Init and not Init at once. So the condition of F5 is met, and F5 asks for the redundancy to be proven. The explicit clause was already there in pass 5 (p5.lean:1166), so 'add' is satisfied, but 'prove' is not. The module has no such lemma. `grep -n -i redundan Ern/MM03.lean` finds only derive_compat_redundant, canWrite3_excl_redundant and issue_disjoint_redundant, so the module proves redundancies elsewhere but not this one. transfer_footprints_disjoint (2417-2421) only projects the explicit clause (`.1.2.2.2.2.1`). Its docstring and the TransferPre docstring (1157-1158) cite F5 but do not mention the redundancy. Decision (6) says 'nothing added' and does not mention it either. The tx0 docstring (9155-9156) itself names both causes of the rejection ('the footprints overlap (F5), and the destination is initialised'). I reproduced the one-line proof myself and it compiles with axioms [propext, Quot.sound].
FIX In formal/Ern/MM03.lean, right after transfer_footprints_disjoint (line 2421), add:
/-- F5: the clause `¬ overlap s.P src dst` of `TransferPre` is redundant. It follows from clause 1 (source initialised) and clause 2 (destination without an `Init` leaf). It is kept explicit (F5: nothing removed). -/
theorem transfer_overlap_redundant {s : S3} {src dst : Nat}
    (h1 : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, s.I l = .init)
    (h2 : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) : ¬ overlap s.P src dst :=
  fun ⟨l, hl, hl'⟩ => h2 l hl' (h1 l hl)
Also cite `transfer_overlap_redundant` in the TransferPre docstring at the F5 mention. In report section (6), replace 'nothing added' with: the explicit clause was already present; it is redundant with clauses 1 and 2 (transfer_overlap_redundant); nothing removed.

===== F356 V1 confirmed minor
TITLE F6 non-vacuity cases (pv*) have no positive twin for any of their rejections
REASONING Step 5 of the brief (task_mm03_p6.md:38) requires 'F7 et cas, avec un jumeau positif pour chaque rejet', and line 47 lists the F6 case with 'paramètre libéré puis accès tenté → reject'. The pv block (MM03.lean:9173-9190) has five rejections: Write3Step 0 [0], Read3Step 0 [0] and DeriveStep 0 0 .modify on releaseEff pv0 1, and Write3Step 1 [0] and Write3Step 0 [0] on releaseEff pv1 2. Its only `.ok` steps are ReleaseStep and EnterStep, which are not the rejected accesses accepted in a changed situation. The pv docstring (9165-9172) names no twin. /-! ## O3 `release` (MM-03.3 §3, A6) -/

/-- Effect of `release(authority)` (MM-03.3 §3, O3; A6: end of a temporary access): the
authority becomes inactive. F4: an authority held by a place `q` leaves the anchors of `q` in the
same transition. -/
def releaseEff (s : S3) (a : Nat) : S3 := match s.A[a]? with
  | some x => { s with
      A := s.A.set a { x with active := false }
      D := fun q => if x.holder = .place q then (s.D q).filter (· != a) else s.D q }
  | none => s

/-- Right of the current frame on a holder (C4): the holder is the current frame, or a place on
which the current frame has exercisable `Modify` (`HasRight`, B2). -/
def HolderRight (s : S3) : Holder → Prop
  | .frame f => f = s.top
  | .place p => HasRight s .modify p

instance (s : S3) (h : Holder) : Decidable (HolderRight s h) := by
  cases h <;> unfold HolderRight <;> infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `release` (MM-03.3 §3, O3), in order: 1 active authority; 2 no active
descendant; 3 no usable place has `a` as anchor, except the place that holds `a`, whose anchor
`a` is removed by the release (F4); C4: the authority is derived, an authority
without origin is rejected, and its holder is the current frame or a place on which the current
frame has exercisable `Modify` (`HolderRight`). O3.4 (guarantees of associated abstractions) is
not represented in the kernel. -/
def ReleasePre (s : S3) (a : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Active a ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, a ∈ s.ancs j → ¬ s.Active j) ∧
  (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → a ∈ s.D q → (s.A[a]?).map (·.holder) = some (.place q)) ∧
  OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun y => y.origin ≠ none ∧ HolderRight s y.holder) False

instance (s : S3) (a : Nat) : Decidable (ReleasePre s a) := by unfold ReleasePre; infer_instance

/-- `release` as a relation (MM-03.3 §3, O3). -/
def ReleaseStep (a : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (ReleasePre s a) (releaseEff s a)

/-- Holder within the value at `q` (A4): a place that is `q` or one of its parts. -/
def heldIn (P : List Place) (q : Nat) : Holder → Prop
  | .place r => partOf P r q
  | .frame _ => False

instance (P : List Place) (q : Nat) (h : Holder) : Decidable (heldIn P q h) := by
  cases h <;> unfold heldIn <;> infer_instance

/-- Effect of `transfer(source, destination)` (MM-03.3 §3, O4; A4; A5): the destination becomes

the destination and leave the source and its parts; every authority held by the source or one
of its parts is now held by the destination (A4); every place owned by the source or one of its
parts is now owned by the destination, without moving (A5). -/

/-- Preconditions of `depend` (MM-03.3 §3, O5), in order: result place usable (MM-03.3.1);
1 valid anchor; 5 non-escape (MM-03.3.6); B3: exercisable `Modify` on the result; C1: the frame
of the effective anchor is the frame of the result or an ancestor of it (`EffAnchorOK`). O5.2
(real origin of the rights or storage) is not representable: the state does not relate a value
to the origin of its content. O5.3 and O5.4 hold by construction. -/
def DependPre (s : S3) (q x : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Usable q ∧ s.Active x ∧ NoEscape s x (s.pframe q) ∧ HasRight s .modify q ∧
    EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)

instance (s : S3) (q x : Nat) : Decidable (DependPre s q x) := by
  unfold DependPre; infer_instance

def DependStep (q x : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=

/-! ## F4 `store` -/

/-- Effect of `store a p` (F4), the write of a reference into a value: `a` is now held by the
place `p`; `a` joins the anchors of `p`; the leaves of `p` become `Init`. -/
def storeEff (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : S3 := match s.A[a]? with
  | some y => { s with
      A := s.A.set a { y with holder := .place p }
      D := fun q => if q = p then s.D p ++ [a] else s.D q
      I := fun l => if l ∈ footprint s.P p then .init else s.I l }

/-- Preconditions of `store a p` (F4), in order: `a` active, derived (`a.origin ≠ none`), held by
the current frame; `p` usable; exercisable `Modify` on `p` (B2, `HasRight`); `a` covers no leaf
of `p` nor of its owned storage, transitively (A5, `OwnedIn`); `AnchorOrder` for the added

of its ancestors. No inverse operation exists (F4). -/

  OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.origin ≠ none ∧ y.holder = .frame s.top) False ∧
  s.Usable p ∧ HasRight s .modify p ∧

  ⟨.ok (by decide), by decide, by decide, by decide⟩

/-! ## Protection of the parameters of a call (F6) -/

/-- `call_protects_params_safe` as stated by F6, transitive form, as a predicate on a state: for a
stack `G ++ f :: F₀`, the current frame being `f` or a frame called by `f` transitively, every
authority exercisable by the current frame (A2, B2) that covers a leaf of the footprint of a
`Modify` authority of `callParams f` is that authority or one of its descendants, whether the
parameter is active or not. It concerns safe accesses only: neither raw pointers nor suspension
are represented. -/
def CallProtects (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Frames) (f : Nat) (F₀ : Frames), s.F = G ++ f :: F₀ →
    ∀ p ∈ s.callParams f, ∀ y : Authority, s.A[p]? = some y → y.mode = .modify →
      ∀ (b : Nat) (m : Mode), s.ExercisableAt b m → ∀ l ∈ y.footprint, l ∈ s.afp b →
        b = p ∨ p ∈ s.ancs b

/-- The direct form of `CallProtects` (F6): the current frame is `f`. -/
def CallProtectsDirect (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (f : Nat) (F₀ : Frames), s.F = f :: F₀ →
    ∀ p ∈ s.callParams f, ∀ y : Authority, s.A[p]? = some y → y.mode = .modify →
      ∀ (b : Nat) (m : Mode), s.ExercisableAt b m → ∀ l ∈ y.footprint, l ∈ s.afp b →
        b = p ∨ p ∈ s.ancs b

theorem CallProtects.direct {s : S3} (h : CallProtects s) : CallProtectsDirect s :=
  fun f F₀ hF => h [] f F₀ hF

theorem S3.ExercisableAt.lt {s : S3} {b : Nat} {m : Mode} (h : s.ExercisableAt b m) :
    b < s.A.length := by
  cases h <;> exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›

/-- The condition of `CallProtects` for one parameter `p`, read on the authorities of `A` and on
both modes: decidable form. -/
def ParamProtected (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop :=
  (s.A[p]?).map (·.mode) = some .modify →
    ∀ b ∈ List.range s.A.length, (s.ExercisableAt b .observe ∨ s.ExercisableAt b .modify) →
      ∀ l ∈ s.afp p, l ∈ s.afp b → b = p ∨ p ∈ s.ancs b

instance (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (ParamProtected s p) := by
  unfold ParamProtected; infer_instance

/-- `CallProtects` holds when every parameter of every frame of the stack is protected
(`ParamProtected`): a decidable sufficient condition, used on concrete states. -/
theorem callProtects_of_check {s : S3}
    (hchk : ∀ f ∈ s.F, ∀ p ∈ s.callParams f, ParamProtected s p) : CallProtects s := by
  intro G f F₀ hF p hp y hy hm b m hex l hl hlb
  have hf : f ∈ s.F := by rw [hF]; exact List.mem_append_right _ (List.mem_cons_self ..)
  exact hchk f hf p hp (by rw [hy]; simp [hm]) b (List.mem_range.2 hex.lt)
    (by cases m with | observe => exact .inl hex | modify => exact .inr hex) l
    (by simp only [S3.afp, hy]; exact hl) hlb

/-- The part of F6 that holds without hypothesis on the call (MM-03.3.5; I1): while an active
`Modify` authority `p` covers a leaf `l`, every authority with a present effective mode on `l` is
`p` or one of its descendants. It says nothing once `p` is released, nor of authorities that are
exercisable without an effective mode on `l`. -/
theorem call_params_effective_protected {s : S3} (h1 : I1 s) {p b l : Nat} {y : Authority}
    (hp : s.A[p]? = some y) (ya : y.active = true) (hm : y.mode = .modify) (hl : l ∈ y.footprint)
    (hb : effective s b l ≠ none) : b = p ∨ p ∈ s.ancs b := by
  by_cases e : b = p
  · exact .inl e
  by_cases hpb : p ∈ s.ancs b
  · exact .inr hpb
  cases he : effective s b l with
  | none => exact absurd he hb
  | some mb =>
    obtain ⟨x, hx, xa, xl, ex⟩ := effective_some he
    by_cases hbp : b ∈ s.ancs p
    · have hd : Mode.modify ∈ descModes s b l := mem_descModes.2 ⟨p, y, hp, ya, hl, hbp, hm⟩
      rcases effOf_cases ex with ⟨h0, -⟩ | ⟨-, hn, -⟩
      · simp [h0] at hd
      · exact absurd hd hn
    · have := (h1 b p x y l e hx hp xa ya xl hl hbp hpb).2
      rw [hm] at this; cases this

/-- F6 is not provable as stated: a counterexample on a reached state, where the caller passes an
authority and one of its descendants. Frame 1: local 0, of root 0; the caller derives 1, `Modify`
on 0, then 2, `Modify` on 0 from 1, and calls with `[1, 2]`. In frame 2, the parameter 1 is
exercisable, covers the leaf 0 of the parameter 2, and is its ancestor, not a descendant. After
the callee releases 2, it writes the leaf 0 through 1. -/
def cp0 : S3 := deriveEff (deriveEff (enter1 [(none, none, 0)]) 0 0 .modify) 1 0 .modify
def cp1 : S3 := enterEff cp0 [1, 2] []
theorem call_protects_params_safe_fails_param :
    Reachable K0 [] cp1 ∧ ¬ CallProtects cp1 ∧
      ReleaseStep 2 cp1 (.ok (releaseEff cp1 2)) ∧ ¬ CallProtects (releaseEff cp1 2) ∧
      Write3Step 1 [0] (releaseEff cp1 2) (.ok (write3Eff (releaseEff cp1 2) [0])) := by
  have hr : Reachable K0 [] cp1 := .enter (.derive (.derive (.enter (.init (by decide))
    (.ok (by decide))) (.ok (by decide))) (.ok (by decide))) (.ok (by decide))
  have key : ∀ s : S3, s.F = [2, 1, 0] → s.callParams 2 = [1, 2] → s.ExercisableAt 1 .modify →
      (s.A[2]?).map (fun y => (y.mode, y.footprint)) = some (.modify, [0]) → s.afp 1 = [0] →
      s.ancs 1 = [0] → ¬ CallProtects s := by
    intro s hF hc hex h2 h1 ha h
    obtain ⟨y, hy, e⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.1 h2
    simp only [Prod.mk.injEq] at e
    have := h.direct 2 [1, 0] hF 2 (by rw [hc]; decide) y hy e.1 1 .modify hex 0 (by rw [e.2]; decide)
      (by rw [h1]; decide)
    rw [ha] at this; simp at this
  exact ⟨hr, key _ (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide),
    .ok (by decide), key _ (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide),
    .ok (by decide)⟩

/-- F6 is not provable as stated: a counterexample on a reached state, through owned storage
(A5; A2, held authorities). Frame 1: value 0, of root 0 held by frame 1, which owns the storage
1, of root 1 held by the place 0. The caller derives 2, `Modify` on 1 from the root 1, and 3,
`Modify` on 0, and calls with `[2, 3]`. In frame 2, the root 1, held by the place 0 on which the
parameter 3 has effective `Modify`, is exercisable and covers the leaf 1 of the parameter 2, of
which it is the origin. After the callee releases 2, it writes the leaf 1 through the root 1. -/
def co0 : S3 :=
  deriveEff (deriveEff (enter1 [(none, none, 0), (none, some 0, 0)]) 1 1 .modify) 0 0 .modify
def co1 : S3 := enterEff co0 [2, 3] []
theorem call_protects_params_safe_fails_owned :
    Reachable K0 [] co1 ∧ ¬ CallProtects co1 ∧
      ReleaseStep 2 co1 (.ok (releaseEff co1 2)) ∧ ¬ CallProtects (releaseEff co1 2) ∧
      Write3Step 1 [1] (releaseEff co1 2) (.ok (write3Eff (releaseEff co1 2) [1])) := by
  have hr : Reachable K0 [] co1 := .enter (.derive (.derive (.enter (.init (by decide))
    (.ok (by decide))) (.ok (by decide))) (.ok (by decide))) (.ok (by decide))
  have key : ∀ s : S3, s.F = [2, 1, 0] → s.callParams 2 = [2, 3] → s.ExercisableAt 1 .modify →
      (s.A[2]?).map (fun y => (y.mode, y.footprint)) = some (.modify, [1]) → s.afp 1 = [1] →
      s.ancs 1 = [] → ¬ CallProtects s := by
    intro s hF hc hex h2 h1 ha h
    obtain ⟨y, hy, e⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.1 h2
    simp only [Prod.mk.injEq] at e
    have := h.direct 2 [1, 0] hF 2 (by rw [hc]; decide) y hy e.1 1 .modify hex 1 (by rw [e.2]; decide)
      (by rw [h1]; decide)
    rw [ha] at this; simp at this
  exact ⟨hr, key _ (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide),
    .ok (by decide), key _ (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide),
    .ok (by decide)⟩

/-! ## New cases of pass 6 -/

/-! ### Nested arena with a child value (F1) -/

/-- An arena nested in a block issued to a value distinct from the parent arena value (F1: the
child arena value is the holder of its `internal`, the block). Frame 1: 0 parent arena value,
1 allocator value, 2 child arena value; storage 3 with parts 4 and 5, owned by 0, of root 3; the
parent issues the block 4 on `[4]` to 2; `newArena 4 4` registers the child on the part 4. The
`reset` of the parent is rejected while the child lives (expected: reject); after the `endUse` of
the child value, which releases the block, it is accepted (expected: `ok`). -/
def na0 : S3 := enter1 [(none, none, 0), (none, none, 0), (none, none, 0)]
def na1 : S3 :=
  allocEff (write3Eff na0 [1]) 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 3, none, 0), (some 3, none, 0)]
def na2 : S3 := newArenaEff na1 3 3
def arNa : Arena := ⟨3, 3, [4, 5], []⟩
def na3 : S3 := arenaSet (issueEff na2 arNa [4] 2).1 0 (issueEff na2 arNa [4] 2).2
def na4 : S3 := newArenaEff na3 4 4
example : NewArenaStep 3 3 na1 (.ok na2) := .ok (by decide)
example : IssueAt K0 0 0 [4] 2 na2 (.ok na3) :=
  .ok (ar := arNa) (by decide) (.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide))
example : NewArenaStep 4 4 na3 (.ok na4) := .ok (by decide)
example : na4.arenas.map (arenaValue na4) = [some 0, some 2] := by decide
example : ResetAtStep K0 0 0 na4 .reject := .reject (by decide)
example : EndUseStep K0 2 na4 (.ok (endUseEff na4 2)) := .ok (by decide)
example : ¬ (endUseEff na4 2).Active 4 := by decide
example : ResetAtStep K0 0 0 (endUseEff na4 2) (.ok (resetAtEff (endUseEff na4 2) 0)) :=
  .ok (by decide)

/-! ### Arena on a local buffer (F1, F2, F4) -/

/-- An arena whose storage is a local buffer of the callee, administered by a derived authority
stored into the arena value. Frame 1: 0 result; it derives 1, `Modify` on 0, and calls. Frame 2:
1 arena value, 2 buffer with parts 3 and 4, 5 and 6 block destinations, 7 another local. The

`[4]` (expected: `ok` for each). The transfer of the arena value to the caller's result is

theorem canWrite3_excl_redundant {s : S3} (h1 : I1 s) {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat}
    (hw : canWrite3 s a ls) : ∀ p ∈ ls, ∀ b, b ≠ a → effective s b p = none :=
  fun p hp _ hb => effective_exclusive h1 (Ne.symm hb) (hw.2 p hp).1

/-! ## Arena (MM-03.3 §6, A10) -/

/-- The place of the arena value: the holder of `internal` (F1, replacing the owner of the storage
of A10 and D3). -/
def arenaValue (s : S3) (ar : Arena) : Option Nat :=
  match s.A[ar.internal]? with
  | some y =>
    match y.holder with
    | .place v => some v
    | .frame _ => none
  | none => none

/-- Metadata leaves of the arena: the footprint of the arena value (A10). -/
def metaLeaves (s : S3) (ar : Arena) : List Nat :=
  match arenaValue s ar with
  | some v => footprint s.P v
  | none => []

/-- Arena invariant (MM-03.3 §6; A10; D3; F1; F2). Clauses of §6: issued regions within the
administered storage (the footprint of `internal`); two simultaneously valid issued regions
disjoint; available regions disjoint from the still distributed ones; added: available regions
within the storage. Clause of A10: each emission is a `Modify` authority derived from `internal`
on its region. F2: the storage is a place of `P`, owned by anything (a local, a static, an
allocated root, a block): the ownership clause of A10 is removed. F1: `internal` is a `Modify`
authority held by a place, the arena value, and covers exactly the footprint of the storage. -/
def ArenaInv (s : S3) (ar : Arena) : Prop :=
  (∀ l ∈ ar.available, l ∈ s.afp ar.internal) ∧
  (∀ e ∈ ar.issued, ∀ l ∈ e.1, l ∈ s.afp ar.internal) ∧
  ar.issued.Pairwise (fun e e' => s.Active e.2 → s.Active e'.2 → ∀ l ∈ e.1, l ∉ e'.1) ∧
  (∀ e ∈ ar.issued, s.Active e.2 → ∀ l ∈ e.1, l ∉ ar.available) ∧
  (∀ e ∈ ar.issued, ∃ y, s.A[e.2]? = some y ∧ y.origin = some ar.internal ∧
    y.footprint = e.1 ∧ y.mode = .modify) ∧
  ar.storage < s.P.length ∧
  (∃ (y : Authority) (v : Nat), s.A[ar.internal]? = some y ∧ y.mode = .modify ∧
    y.holder = .place v) ∧
  (∀ l, l ∈ s.afp ar.internal ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P ar.storage)

/-- Right to update the metadata of the arena (A10; C6, aligned with `ProviderRight`): exercisable
`Modify` on the arena value, or an authority `via` exercisable at `Observe` (B2) with a present
effective mode on every metadata leaf, all `SharedMutable` (a `writeShared`, A9), with valid
dependencies. -/
def MetaRight (k : K) (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (via : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (arenaValue s ar) (fun v => HasRight s .modify v) False ∨
  (s.ExercisableAt via .observe ∧ arenaValue s ar ≠ none ∧
    ∀ l ∈ metaLeaves s ar, effective s via l ≠ none ∧ k.SharedMutable l ∧ DepsValid s l)

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (via : Nat) :
    Decidable (MetaRight k s ar via) := by
  unfold MetaRight; infer_instance

/-- Static preconditions of `arena.issue(region)` (MM-03.3 §6; A10): metadata right (A10); the
region lies in the storage administered by `internal`; the destination `dst` of the block is
usable, exercisable in `Modify` (A2) and holds no initialised value. -/
def IssueStatic (k : K) (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (via : Nat) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :
    Prop :=
  MetaRight k s ar via ∧ s.Active ar.internal ∧ (∀ l ∈ region, l ∈ s.afp ar.internal) ∧
  s.Usable dst ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init)

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (via : Nat)
    (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Decidable (IssueStatic k s ar via region dst) := by
  unfold IssueStatic; infer_instance

/-- The region is available (MM-03.3 §6): otherwise `issue` fails (A10). -/
def Avail (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) : Prop := ∀ l ∈ region, l ∈ ar.available

instance (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) : Decidable (Avail ar region) := by
  unfold Avail; infer_instance

/-- The abstraction has, through `internal`, effective `Modify` on the region (MM-03.3 §6:
the abstraction has the authority needed to distribute the region). The
disjointness from active emissions is removed (A11): it follows from this right
(`issue_disjoint_redundant`). -/
def IssueRight (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ l ∈ region, effective s ar.internal l = some .modify

instance (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) : Decidable (IssueRight s ar region) := by
  unfold IssueRight; infer_instance

/-- Effect of `arena.issue(region)` (MM-03.3 §6; A10): a `Modify` block derived from `internal`
on the region, held by the destination value; the destination and the metadata become `Init`;
the region leaves `available` and joins `issued`. -/
def issueEff (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : S3 × Arena :=
  ({ s.addAuth ⟨.modify, some ar.internal, region, .place dst, true⟩ with
      I := fun l => if l ∈ footprint s.P dst ∨ l ∈ metaLeaves s ar then .init else s.I l },
   { ar with
      available := ar.available.filter fun l => decide (l ∉ region)
      issued := (region, s.A.length) :: ar.issued })

/-! ## Arenas in the state (D3) -/

/-- The state with the entry `i` of `arenas` replaced by `ar` (D3). -/
def arenaSet (s : S3) (i : Nat) (ar : Arena) : S3 := { s with arenas := s.arenas.set i ar }

/-- Preconditions of `newArena storage internal` (D3, F1, F2), in order. Kept from D3: exercisable
`Modify` on `storage`; `storage` usable. F1: `internal`, named by the caller, is active, `Modify`,
exercisable at `Modify` (B2), and held by a place, the arena value; the footprint of `internal` is
the footprint of `storage`; no live arena already has `internal` as `internal`. F1 removes the
guard by place index of D3 and the kind of `internal`; F2 removes the ownership of the storage
(A10): the storage may be a local, a static, an allocated root or a block. -/
def NewArenaPre (s : S3) (storage internal : Nat) : Prop :=
  HasRight s .modify storage ∧ s.Usable storage ∧
    OptP (s.A[internal]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.mode = .modify ∧ y.holder.isPlace = true)
      False ∧
    s.ExercisableAt internal .modify ∧
    (∀ l ∈ s.afp internal, l ∈ footprint s.P storage) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P storage, l ∈ s.afp internal) ∧
    (∀ ar ∈ s.arenas, s.Active ar.internal → ar.internal ≠ internal)

instance (s : S3) (storage internal : Nat) : Decidable (NewArenaPre s storage internal) := by
  unfold NewArenaPre; infer_instance

/-- Effect of `newArena storage internal` (D3; F1): a new entry, the whole storage available,
nothing issued. -/
def newArenaEff (s : S3) (storage internal : Nat) : S3 :=
  { s with arenas := s.arenas ++ [⟨storage, internal, s.afp internal, []⟩] }

/-- `newArena storage internal : ok | reject` as a relation (D3; F1). -/
def NewArenaStep (storage internal : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (NewArenaPre s storage internal) (newArenaEff s storage internal)

/-- `arena.issue` on the entry `i` of the state (MM-03.3 §6; A10; D3): the step `IssueStep` of the
recorded arena, whose new logical state is written back; a missing entry is rejected. An entry
whose `internal` is released is rejected by `IssueStatic`, which asks it active. -/
inductive IssueAt (k : K) (i via : Nat) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) (s : S3) :
    AOutcome → Prop where
  | ok {ar : Arena} {s' : S3} {ar' : Arena} : s.arenas[i]? = some ar →
      IssueStep k ar via region dst s (.ok s' ar') → IssueAt k i via region dst s (.ok (arenaSet s' i ar'))
  | fail {ar : Arena} {s' : S3} {ar' : Arena} : s.arenas[i]? = some ar →
      IssueStep k ar via region dst s (.fail s' ar') → IssueAt k i via region dst s (.fail s)
  | reject {ar : Arena} : s.arenas[i]? = some ar → IssueStep k ar via region dst s .reject →
      IssueAt k i via region dst s .reject
  | none : s.arenas[i]? = none → IssueAt k i via region dst s .reject

/-- `reachable_access_invariant` (MM-03.3 §10; B8, C1, C2, D3): every reached state satisfies `WF3`,
`Inv3`, and `ArenaInv` for every live arena. Conditional on the obligation `DDSound k` of
`DeclaredDisjoint` (MM-03.3.8), used by `split`. -/
theorem reachable_access_invariant_underDD {k : K} (hdd : DDSound k) {statics : Statics} {s : S3}
    (h : Reachable k statics s) :
    WF3 s ∧ Inv3 s ∧ ∀ ar ∈ s.arenas, s.Active ar.internal → ArenaInv s ar :=
  let h' := reachable_invariants hdd h

/-- `reachable_no_dangling` (C2; MM-03.3 §10; D3): in every reached state, no active authority
covers a leaf of a place that is not usable. Under `DDSound k` (MM-03.3.8). -/
theorem reachable_no_dangling {k : K} (hdd : DDSound k) {statics : Statics} {s : S3}
    (h : Reachable k statics s) :
    NoDangling s :=
  (reachable_access_invariant_underDD hdd h).2.1.nd

/-- `live_arena_storage_usable` (F2): in every reached state, the storage of a live arena is
usable. A corollary of `NoDangling` (C2): `internal` is active and covers the footprint of the
storage (`ArenaInv`, F1), which has a leaf. Under `DDSound k` (MM-03.3.8). -/
theorem live_arena_storage_usable {k : K} (hdd : DDSound k) {statics : Statics} {s : S3}
    (h : Reachable k statics s) : ∀ ar ∈ s.arenas, s.Active ar.internal → s.Usable ar.storage := by

    hi.2.2.2.2.2.1

(MM-03.3.8). -/
theorem exitFrame_no_dangling_reachable {k : K} (hdd : DDSound k) {statics : Statics} {s s' : S3} {f : Nat}

/-- `StaticPinnedBottom k s` (C5, F3), obligation on the static pinning `K.Pinned`: every leaf
covered by `K.Pinned` belongs to a place owned directly by the base frame, the last of the stack
(frame 0 on reached states, `reachable_base_owns_statics`). F3 replaces the transitive ownership
of C5 by direct ownership. Dynamic pinning (`pin`, `unpin`) is not concerned. -/
def StaticPinnedBottom (k : K) (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ l, k.Pinned l → ∃ (q : Nat) (pl : Place), l ∈ footprint s.P q ∧ s.P[q]? = some pl ∧
    pl.owner = .frame (s.F.getLastD 0)

/-- A place has at most one owning frame (A5). -/
theorem OwnedByFrame.unique {P : List Place} {f g q : Nat} (h : OwnedByFrame P f q)
    (h' : OwnedByFrame P g q) : f = g := by
  induction h with
  | @frame q pl hpl ho =>
    cases h' with
    | frame hpl' ho' => rw [hpl] at hpl'; cases hpl'; rw [ho] at ho'; cases ho'; rfl
    | place hpl' ho' _ => rw [hpl] at hpl'; cases hpl'; rw [ho] at ho'; cases ho'
  | @place q o pl hpl ho _ ih =>
    cases h' with
    | frame hpl' ho' => rw [hpl] at hpl'; cases hpl'; rw [ho] at ho'; cases ho'
    | place hpl' ho' h'' => rw [hpl] at hpl'; cases hpl'; rw [ho] at ho'; cases ho'; exact ih h''

/-- `static_pinned_never_exits` (C5; F3): under `StaticPinnedBottom`, no frame exit meets a
statically pinned leaf: a place that stops being usable at the exit covers no leaf of
`K.Pinned`. -/
theorem static_pinned_never_exits {k : K} {s : S3} {f : Nat} {F₀ : Frames} (hwf : WF3 s)
    (hsp : StaticPinnedBottom k s) (hF : s.F = f :: F₀) (hne : F₀ ≠ []) :
    ∀ q, s.Usable q → ¬ ({ s with F := F₀ } : S3).Usable q →
      ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, ¬ k.Pinned l := by

  have hof := exit_owned_of_usable hF hq hq'
  obtain ⟨q', pl₀, hl', hq₀, ho₀⟩ := hsp l hpin
  have hob : OwnedByFrame s.P (s.F.getLastD 0) q' := .frame hq₀ ho₀
  obtain ⟨-, -, hlq⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
  obtain ⟨-, -, hlq'⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl'
  obtain ⟨pl, pq, hpl, hpq, e⟩ := hwf.ownerOf hlq
  obtain ⟨pl', pq', hpl', hpq', e'⟩ := hwf.ownerOf hlq'
  rw [hpl] at hpl'; cases hpl'
  have hfb := (hof.of_owner hpq hpl e).unique (hob.of_owner hpq' hpl e')
  obtain ⟨g, F₁, rfl⟩ : ∃ g F₁, F₀ = g :: F₁ := by
    cases F₀ with
    | nil => exact absurd rfl hne
    | cons g F₁ => exact ⟨g, F₁, rfl⟩

/-! ## Abstract reads and writes (MM-03.3 §5) -/

/-- Ordinary read condition of a leaf by authority `a` (MM-03.3 §5, `canRead3`): an effective
authority permits observation, the leaf is initialised, the needed dependencies are valid. The
type and storage contract is not represented. -/
def CanReadLeaf (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : Prop :=
  effective s a p ≠ none ∧ s.I p = .init ∧ DepsValid s p

instance (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : Decidable (CanReadLeaf s a p) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

/-- `canRead3` (MM-03.3 §5): ordinary read of leaves `ls` by authority `a`, exercisable at
`Observe` (B2). -/
def canRead3 (s : S3) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) : Prop :=
  s.ExercisableAt a .observe ∧ ∀ p ∈ ls, CanReadLeaf s a p

instance (s : S3) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) : Decidable (canRead3 s a ls) := by
  unfold canRead3; infer_instance

/-- `read3` as a relation (MM-03.3 §5): a read does not change the state. -/
def Read3Step (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (canRead3 s a ls) s

/-- `canWrite3` (MM-03.3 §5): `a` exercisable at `Modify` (B2); on each leaf, effective
`Modify` of `a` and needed dependencies valid. The clause "no other ordinary authority with an
incompatible effective right" is removed (A11): it follows from the first under I1
(`canWrite3_excl_redundant`). The type and storage condition is not represented. -/
def canWrite3 (s : S3) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) : Prop :=
  s.ExercisableAt a .modify ∧ ∀ p ∈ ls, effective s a p = some .modify ∧ DepsValid s p

instance (s : S3) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) : Decidable (canWrite3 s a ls) := by
  unfold canWrite3; infer_instance

/-- Effect of a write (MM-03.3 §5): written leaves become `Init`. -/
def write3Eff (s : S3) (ls : List Nat) : S3 := { s with I := fun p => if p ∈ ls then .init else s.I p }

    subst this

theorem store_preserves {s s' : S3} {a p : Nat} (hwf : WF3 s) (hinv : Inv3base s)
    (h : StoreStep a p s (.ok s')) : WF3 s' ∧ Inv3base s' := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  obtain ⟨y, hy, ya, ho, -⟩ := store_pre_auth hpre

theorem store_preserves_anchorOrder {s s' : S3} {a p : Nat} (hwf : WF3 s) (hao : AnchorOrder s)
    (h : StoreStep a p s (.ok s')) : AnchorOrder s' := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  obtain ⟨y, hy, -, ho, -⟩ := store_pre_auth hpre

theorem store_preserves_noDangling {s s' : S3} {a p : Nat} (hnd : NoDangling s)
    (h : StoreStep a p s (.ok s')) : NoDangling s' := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  obtain ⟨y, hy, -⟩ := store_pre_auth hpre

theorem store_effAnchorOK {s : S3} {a p : Nat} {y : Authority} (hwf : WF3 s)
    (hy : s.A[a]? = some y) (ho : y.origin ≠ none) (x : Nat) (fd : Option Nat) :
    EffAnchorOK (storeEff s a p) x fd ↔ EffAnchorOK s x fd := by
  have sk := store_skel s a p

theorem store_root_rejected {s : S3} {a p : Nat} {y : Authority} (hy : s.A[a]? = some y)
    (ho : y.origin = none) : StoreStep a p s .reject :=
  .reject fun h => by
    obtain ⟨y', hy', -, ho', -⟩ := store_pre_auth h

theorem exists_mem_footprint {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) :
    ∀ n q, s.P.length - q < n → q < s.P.length → ∃ l, l ∈ footprint s.P q
  | 0, _, h, _ => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
  | n + 1, q, hn, hq => by

theorem release_D_mem {s : S3} {a q y : Nat} {x : Authority} (hx : s.A[a]? = some x)
    (hy : y ∈ (releaseEff s a).D q) : y ∈ s.D q ∧ (y = a → x.holder ≠ .place q) := by
  rw [releaseEff_eq hx] at hy; simp only at hy
  split at hy

theorem chain_trans {org : Nat → Option Nat} (hlt : ∀ i o, org i = some o → o < i) :
    ∀ n i, i < n → ∀ r, r ∈ chain org i → ∀ o ∈ chain org r, o ∈ chain org i
  | 0, _, h, _, _, _, _ => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
  | n + 1, i, hi, r, hr, o, ho => by

theorem arena_dies_with_internal {k : K} {s s' : S3} {ar : Arena} {v : Nat}
    (hv : arenaValue s ar = some v) (h : EndUseStep k v s (.ok s')) :
    ¬ s'.Active ar.internal := by
  obtain ⟨⟨hu, -⟩, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h

theorem transfer_footprints_disjoint {k : K} {s s' : S3} {src dst : Nat}
    (h : TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s')) : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, l ∉ footprint s.P dst :=

/-- Preconditions of `transfer` (MM-03.3 §3, O4), in order: source usable (MM-03.3.1) and
1 initialised; 2 destination usable, without an `Init` leaf, sharing no leaf with the source (F5:
the footprints of source and destination are disjoint, the clause `¬ overlap`, redundant with
clauses 1 and 2 by `transfer_overlap_redundant`),
and still usable once it owns the source's storage (no ownership cycle); exercisable `Modify`
on the source and on the destination (B2); 4 no active derived
access on the source other than those it holds; 5 anchors of the value valid; 6 non-escape
(MM-03.3.6) towards the destination's frame, for the anchors of the value and of the usable
places it owns, whose frame changes with it (A5), each frame read after the transfer (B7);
7 no leaf of the source pinned, statically
(`Pinned`, MM-03.3.8) or dynamically (A8); B8 on the effective anchor (C1): for every dependent
usable after the transfer, if its effective anchor moves with the value, or if the dependent
itself moves (the destination, or a place the value owns), the frame of the effective anchor is
the dependent's frame or an ancestor of it, both frames read after the transfer
(`EffAnchorOK`). O4.3 holds by construction. -/
def TransferPre (k : K) (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Usable src ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, s.I l = .init) ∧
  s.Usable dst ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) ∧ ¬ overlap s.P src dst ∧
  HasRight s .modify src ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧
  (transferEff s src dst).Usable dst ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ ActiveDerivedOutside s src j) ∧
  (∀ x ∈ depsOf s src, s.Active x) ∧
  (∀ x ∈ movedDeps s src,
    NoEscape (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe dst)) ∧
  (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, ¬ k.Pinned l ∧ s.pin l = false) ∧
  (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (transferEff s src dst).Usable q →
    ∀ x ∈ (transferEff s src dst).D q,
      (AnchorMoves s src (s.effAnchor x) ∨ q = dst ∨ OwnedWithin s src q) →
      EffAnchorOK (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe q))

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (TransferPre k s src dst) := by
  unfold TransferPre; infer_instance

/-- `transfer` as a relation (MM-03.3 §3, O4). -/
def TransferStep (k : K) (src dst : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (TransferPre k s src dst) (transferEff s src dst)

/-! ## O5 `depend` (MM-03.3 §3) -/

/-- Effect of `depend(result, anchor)` (MM-03.3 §3, O5): the anchor joins the dependencies of
the result place; existing dependencies are kept; propagation to containing values is computed
by `depsOf`. -/
def dependEff (s : S3) (q x : Nat) : S3 :=
  { s with D := fun r => if r = q then s.D q ++ [x] else s.D r }

## (d) Théorèmes non prouvés tels que demandés, et pourquoi

1. **« le cadre 0 possède exactement les emplacements statiques et leur stockage possédé »** (étape 1). `reachable_base_owns_statics` prouve la possession directe : un emplacement a pour propriétaire le cadre 0 si et seulement s'il est un élément statique sans élément propriétaire. Pour un statique possédé par un autre statique (décision 2), la possession transitive par le cadre 0 n'est pas invariante. Témoin `static_not_owned_by_frame0` :
   - un appelé reçoit un paramètre `Modify` dérivé sur le statique 0 ;
   - il exerce la racine du statique 1, détenue par 0 (A2), et transfère 1 vers son local ;
   - après la sortie, le statique 2, possédé par 1, appartient au cadre sorti, et n'est plus utilisable.

   Avec des statiques sans élément propriétaire, l'énoncé direct dit exactement ce que l'étape demande.
2. **Arène imbriquée, « `ok` après `endUse` de l'enfant et de son bloc »** (étape 5). Non réalisable. D3 veut l'`internal` de l'enfant détenu par le propriétaire de son stockage. Or le stockage de l'enfant partage des feuilles avec celui du parent, et deux emplacements qui partagent une feuille ont le même propriétaire (`WF3`, `shared_leaf_same_owner`). L'enfant a donc la valeur arène du parent (`nested_same_value`) : le bloc doit être émis vers cette valeur, et l'`endUse` de l'enfant finit le parent (`arena_dies_with_internal`, appliqué à chaque entrée). Le module le montre sur l'arène imbriquée `nA5` : l'`endUse` de la valeur commune libère les deux `internal`, et le `reset` du parent est alors rejeté. L'impossibilité elle-même est argumentée, pas énoncée comme théorème : elle repose sur `nested_same_value` et sur le fait que `issue` ne change aucun propriétaire. Le module teste la forme réalisable :
   - l'enfant reçoit le bloc émis vers la valeur arène du parent (`nA0`…`nA5`, `nested_reachable`) ;
   - `reset` du parent rejeté tant que l'enfant vit ;
   - `issue` de l'enfant `ok` tant qu'il vit, rejeté après le `release` de son `internal` ;
   - `reset` du parent ensuite `ok`.

   Question (e) 2.
3. **`arena_inv_preserved`** (passe 2, A10) prend maintenant l'hypothèse `hlive` (décision 14). La forme sans elle n'est pas prouvée sous le nouvel `ArenaInv`. La revue n'en a pas construit de contre-exemple sur un état atteint.
4. **Inchangés** : passe 2, (d) 2 (`DDSound` nécessaire), 5 (théorèmes qui réénoncent une précondition ; passe 3, (d) 4) et 6 (pas de totalité) ; passe 3, (d) 2 (`Inv3` seul n'est préservé ni par `transfer`, ni par `enterFrame`, ni par `alloc` : `transfer_not_inv3_preserving`, `enter_not_inv3_preserving`, `alloc_not_inv3_preserving`, dont les témoins satisfont l'`Inv3` complet). La passe 2, (d) 3 (`Reachable` sans arène) est résolue par D3, et la passe 4, (d) 1 (`static_pinned_never_exits` sans contenu sur un état atteint) par D1 (`staticPinned_reached`).
5. **Liste d'arènes non vide « à chaque état vérifié »** (étape 5, cas 16 et n4). L'exécution part de `S3.init []` et introduit l'arène par `alloc` puis `newArena`. Sur `a0`, `a1` et `a2`, où sont vérifiés l'écriture du fournisseur, `alloc` et `newArena`, la liste est donc vide. `case16_reachable` l'énonce non vide à partir de `newArena`, pour `a3` et `a6` à `a11`. Les deux états intermédiaires des `derive` ne sont pas énoncés.

## (e) Questions pour arbitrage

Questions de la passe 4 tranchées : 1 (D1), 2 (D2). Question de la passe 2 encore ouverte : 13 (`WF3` dans la spécification).

Questions nouvelles :

1. **Statiques possédés par un statique** ((c) 2, (d) 1). La composante « élément propriétaire » permet un statique possédé par un autre. Sa racine est alors détenue par son statique propriétaire (A4), il peut quitter la possession du cadre 0 par un transfert, et `StaticPinnedBottom` n'est pas invariant pour lui (témoins `static_not_owned_by_frame0`, `staticPinnedBottom_not_invariant`). Faut-il :
   - interdire l'élément propriétaire dans les statiques, ce qui rend D1 et l'étape 1 vrais mot pour mot ;
   - ou accepter ces conséquences ?
2. **Arènes imbriquées** ((d) 2). La région d'un bloc reste du stockage possédé par la valeur arène du parent : `issue` ne change aucun propriétaire. D3 veut l'`internal` détenu par le propriétaire du stockage. Un enfant a donc la valeur arène de son parent (`nested_same_value`), et son `endUse` finit les deux (`arena_dies_with_internal`, appliqué à chaque entrée). Faut-il :
   - que `issue` donne au destinataire la possession de la région ;
   - que l'`internal` d'une arène imbriquée soit détenu par le destinataire du bloc, et non par le propriétaire du stockage ;
   - ou que le cas d'épreuve finisse l'enfant par `release` de son bloc ?
3. **« ce stockage »** ((c) 11). La garde de `newArena` compare des emplacements. Doit-elle comparer des emplacements ou des feuilles ? Comparer des feuilles rejetterait toute arène imbriquée.
4. **Stockage possédé par un emplacement** ((c) 9). `newArena` l'exige, d'après A10 ; D3 ne l'énumère pas. Est-ce voulu ?
5. **`available` et `issued`** ((c) 7). Restent-ils dans l'entrée, comme le module le fait ?
6. **`newArena` sur une partie qui n'est pas un bloc émis** ((c) 10). D3 nomme l'`internal` d'une racine allouée et celui d'un bloc émis, et ne dit rien des autres stockages. Le module exige une autorité dérivée pour toute partie. Dans `x2`, `newArena 4` sur l'unique partie de la racine 3 est donc rejeté, alors que les trois préconditions de D3 valent et que la racine 3 est une autorité `Modify` détenue par le propriétaire de 4, qui couvre exactement son empreinte. Faut-il :
   - rejeter `newArena` sur une partie que n'administre aucune autorité dérivée, comme le fait le module ? Pour un emplacement racine, le module prend sa racine pour `internal`, que l'emplacement soit alloué, statique ou local.
   - l'accepter, avec pour `internal` l'autorité qui satisfait la clause générale (ici la racine 3) ? Deux arènes vivantes pourraient alors administrer les mêmes feuilles (question 3).
   - ou restreindre `newArena` aux deux cas que D3 nomme, racine allouée et bloc émis ? Le module accepte aujourd'hui aussi une racine statique ou locale possédée par un emplacement.

findings.title: The report still claims F7 (a) blocks until the frame exits, which is unproven and contradicts its own (p) and the review fix
findings.evidence: (e) 2 says: « `store` accepte un cycle qui rend les deux autorités stockées inexerçables jusqu'à la sortie du cadre ». (l) says: « Elles bloquent l'`endUse` des valeurs de nœud et le `reset`, jusqu'à la sortie du cadre ». (n) 1 says: « F7 (a) montre un blocage jusqu'à la sortie de cadre ». Each sentence claims the cycle persists until exitFrame. The module proves only one-step facts at fa8. `progress_cycle_whole_nodes` (MM03.lean:9304) concludes ¬ExercisableAt 7/8 .observe and the rejections of release, endUse and reset in fa8. It proves nothing about later states. Its corrected docstring (cbbfe2f) says « Whether frame 1 can free 7 or 8 before its exit is open (F7: no conclusion of impossibility without proof) ». The report's own (p) (:472) says « Qu'une autre séquence libère 7 ou 8 avant la sortie reste un résultat ouvert : aucune impossibilité n'est démontrée », and the Corrections row (:92) says « la question du blocage reste ouverte ». The brief (task_mm03_p6.md, F7) forbids this: « Aucune conclusion d'impossibilité sans preuve : une séquence non trouvée est un résultat ouvert ». First-review verdict F7 V1 (partly) is fixed in the module docstring but not in these three report passages. The (e) 2 question to the arbiter rests on this unproven premise.
findings.suggested_fix: In (e) 2, (l) and (n) 1, state only what is proven: in fa8 neither 7 nor 8 is exercisable, and release, endUse and reset are rejected one step at a time. Whether a release before the exit is possible is open; refer to (p).

findings.title: store_escape_rejected_at_transfer covers less than (d) 3 and (j) claim: an authority derived from a place-owned local of the current frame is not covered
findings.evidence: Step 3 asks: « une valeur tenant une autorité dérivée d'un local du cadre courant ne peut être transférée vers un cadre plus ancien ». (d) 3 says « Le théorème le prouve pour une autorité ancrée sur la valeur ou un de ses champs, ce que fait store », and (j) says « Vers un cadre plus ancien que celui de son ancre effective, le transfert est rejeté (store_escape_rejected_at_transfer) ». The theorem assumes that the effective anchor is held directly by the frame (`hzf : z.holder = .frame f`). Under A5, the root of a local owned by another local is held by a place, so the theorem excludes authorities derived from such locals. Counterexample I checked: scratchpad/rev13/brief/b3.lean compiles, with axioms [propext, Quot.sound]. hw0 = enterEff (deriveEff (enter1 [(none,none,0)]) 0 0 .modify) [1] [(none,none,0),(none,some 1,0),(none,none,0),(none,none,0)]; hw3 = storeEff (deriveEff (write3Eff hw0 [2]) 3 2 .observe) 6 3. It proves: Reachable K0 [] hw3; TransferStep K0 3 0 hw3 .reject; TransferStep K0 3 4 hw3 (.ok _); 6 ∈ depsOf hw3 3; hw3.F = [2,1,0]; origin of 6 = some 3, the root of local 2 of frame 2; and ∀ z, hw3.A[hw3.effAnchor 6]? = some z → z.holder ≠ .frame 2 (the holder is .place 1). The #eval of the TransferPre clauses gives [true ×12, false]: only the B8/EffAnchorOK clause rejects. The model therefore rejects this escape, but the theorem cannot be applied to it, and the report does not mention the restriction. (c) 11 states the hypothesis but does not flag it as a narrowing of the step-3 demand.
findings.suggested_fix: Either report the restriction in (c) 11, (d) 3 and (j), namely that only authorities whose effective anchor (a root) is held by the frame itself are covered, not those derived from locals owned by a place, with hw3 as the witness. Or restate the hypothesis on the frame of the holder (S3.hframe z.holder = some f), which the arbitrage text supports.
